Dengue Outbreak in 2016 Disrupted Vietnam’s Electrical Equipment Industry

The Vietnamese electrical equipment sector faced significant disruption in 2016 when a widespread dengue fever outbreak struck several industrial zones in the southern provinces. Multiple major factories, including those operated by the local firm VietElec Components, reported absenteeism rates as high as 30% during the peak of the outbreak in July and August that year.

Nguyen Van Thao, Vice Chair of the Vietnam Electrical Manufacturing Association, recalls, “Production schedules were suddenly thrown into disarray. Some assembly lines were forced to halt operations for up to ten days as workers fell ill or were quarantined.” According to the association, the hardest-hit sites were located in Binh Duong and Dong Nai, where clusters of dengue cases emerged among both production and maintenance staff.

Industry analysts estimate that output losses for the sector reached 12% during the third quarter of 2016, with the impact most pronounced among small- and medium-sized enterprises lacking in-house medical support. “This outbreak exposed weaknesses in workplace health infrastructure,” said Le Thi Bao, an independent industry consultant. “Some plants responded quickly by fumigating their premises and distributing mosquito nets, while others struggled due to limited resources.”

Export commitments were also affected, with several companies reporting delays of up to three weeks in fulfilling orders to regional partners. The Vietnam Trade Federation for Electrical Equipment stated in an August 2016 bulletin, “Recovery has begun, but workforce health and productivity remain a concern.”

In the aftermath, most companies introduced annual dengue prevention campaigns and upgraded on-site medical facilities. As one union representative noted, “This event prompted a long-overdue investment in worker health and safety across the industry.”
